newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish finmin welcomes mandatory reserves rise.
newsitem.headline: Polish finmin welcomes mandatory reserves rise.

text.p: Polish Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko on Tuesday welcomed the central bank's decision to increase mandatory reserves on banking deposits, saying the move will help curb inflation.

"The decision will contribute to the stabilisation of the monetary market and it is a factor supporting our anti-inflationary actions," Kolodko told a news briefing. He was speaking before the central bank announced on Tuesday it would not cut official interest rates.
On Monday, The National Bank of Poland raised mandatory reserves on zloty call deposits by three points to 20 percent and on foreign currency deposits by two points to four percent.
It said the rise was needed to keep money supply under control and to counter the rise in foreign currency savings.
The increase is also expected to curb the recent growth of credit action and reduce ballooning domestic demand, which some analysts said showed the Polish economy was overheating.
Some analysts have said the government's plan to cut year-on-year inflation to 13 percent in December from 18.5 percent last year would not be met unless domestic demand was curbed.
